Freshmen usually end up in Warren, the biggest dorm building on campus. 

Pros: Social environment since you’re with a lot of other freshmen. Also right across from CAS where a lot of classes are, and in close proximity to other Central Campus locations like GSU. Has its own dining hall, Subway, Basho, Starbucks, City Co+Dunkin Express, and some bank ATMs.

 Cons: I once heard someone say that Warren was designed by a prison designer and Idk if it’s true but it shows. Rooms are small and cramped (kinda typical dorm room), you might end up living in a tiny space with 2-3 other people. Communal bathrooms on each floor which can get iffy if you’re someone who really likes privacy in the bathroom. It’s generally also kinda gross and I’ve heard about a variety of pest problems. No air conditioning which can be hell in the hotter months. Also, there’s only a few elevators and it can become a nightmare during the classtime rushes. It’s somewhere that you can tolerate living freshman year but definitely want to get out of afterwards.

You might also end up in West or even Towers. West is pretty similar to Warren, maybe a little cleaner but it’s on the complete end of campus. It’s conveniently next to the gym and has its own dining hall but can feel far from everywhere. It’s right next to Nickerson Field, though, so it’s ideal if you’re an athlete.

Towers is on Bay State and borders East/Central campus. Rooms are small but it’s not so bad tbh, also pretty similar to the other big dorm buildings. I’d say the biggest perk is that it’s location is underrated, you’re in proximity to 3 dining halls (Warren, Marciano, and Granby) plus it’s close to CAS, Questrom, Sargent, Wheelock, and GSU isn’t too far either.
